messages.content:
Risk: Emotional Entanglement
Description: Users may develop complex emotional attachments or dependencies on the AI system, potentially affecting mental health andsocial relationships.
Concern: None
Policy: Mental Health & Therapeutic Communication

Candidate ontology classes:
- http://d3fend.mitre.org/ontologies/d3fend.owl#AML.TA0015: Lateral Movement - ATLAS — The adversary is trying to move through your AI environment.

Lateral Movement consists of techniques that adversaries may use to gain access to and control other systems or components in the environment. Adversaries may pivot towards AI Ops infrastructure such as model registries, experiment trackers, vector databases, notebooks, or training pipelines. As the adversary moves through the environment, they may discover means of accessing additional AI-related tools, services, or applications. AI agents may also be a valuable target as they commonly have more permissions than standard user accounts on the system. [found by 2/3 queries]
  Siblings: Command and Control - ATTACK Mobile, Defense Evasion - SPARTA, Lateral Movement - ATTACK Mobile
- http://d3fend.mitre.org/ontologies/d3fend.owl#AML.T0047: AI-Enabled Product or Service - ATLAS — Adversaries may use a product or service that uses artificial intelligence under the hood to gain access to the underlying AI model.
This type of indirect model access may reveal details of the AI model or its inferences in logs or metadata. [found by 2/3 queries]
  Siblings: AI Model Inference API Access - ATLAS, Physical Environment Access - ATLAS, Full AI Model Access - ATLAS
- http://d3fend.mitre.org/ontologies/d3fend.owl#AML.T0011: User Execution - ATLAS — An adversary may rely upon specific actions by a user in order to gain execution.
Users may inadvertently execute unsafe code introduced via [AI Supply Chain Compromise](/techniques/AML.T0010).
Users may be subjected to social engineering to get them to execute malicious code by, for example, opening a malicious document file or link.
  Siblings: LLM Prompt Injection - ATLAS, Command and Scripting Interpreter - ATLAS, AI Agent Tool Invocation - ATLAS
- http://d3fend.mitre.org/ontologies/d3fend.owl#AML.T0073: Impersonation - ATLAS — Adversaries may impersonate a trusted person or organization in order to persuade and trick a target into performing some action on their behalf. For example, adversaries may communicate with victims (via [Phishing](/techniques/AML.T0052), or [Spearphishing via Social Engineering LLM](/techniques/AML.T0052.000)) while impersonating a known sender such as an executive, colleague, or third-party vendor. Established trust can then be leveraged to accomplish an adversary's ultimate goals, possibly against multiple victims.

Adversaries may target resources that are part of the AI DevOps lifecycle, such as model repositories, container registries, and software registries.
  Siblings: Corrupt AI Model - ATLAS, Delay Execution of LLM Instructions - ATLAS, Evade AI Model - ATLAS
- http://d3fend.mitre.org/ontologies/d3fend.owl#AML.T0048: External Harms - ATLAS — Adversaries may abuse their access to a victim system and use its resources or capabilities to further their goals by causing harms external to that system.
These harms could affect the organization (e.g. Financial Harm, Reputational Harm), its users (e.g. User Harm), or the general public (e.g. Societal Harm).
  Siblings: Denial of AI Service - ATLAS, Evade AI Model - ATLAS, Spamming AI System with Chaff Data - ATLAS

axes.rationale: Emotional entanglement risk involves users developing strong attachments to the AI, suggesting a potential for user-driven actions and interactions that are influenced by these emotions.
Emotional entanglement can lead to external harms, such as negative impacts on mental health and social relationships, which are consequences outside the AI system itself.
